To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we replicated 12 out of 14 type 2 diabetes susceptibility loci in the Chinese population and found that the rs10830963 locus was associated with fasting insulin and insulin resistance, while the rs1111875 and rs11196297 loci were associated with fasting insulin.
the variants in the TCF7L2, SLC30A8 and HHEX/IDE genes were associated with type 2 diabetes and with quantitative measures of glucose homoeostatic capacity, but not with the progression of diabetes.

the genetic variants associated with type 2 diabetes risk in Han Chinese were associated with impaired insulin sensitivity and beta‐cell function in nondiabetic individuals, and that the genetic variants were associated with progression to diabetes in nondiabetic relatives.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the genetic basis of type 2 (non-insulin-dependent) diabetes mellitus (T2DM), which has been associated with a number of environmental factors including diet, physical activity and obesity.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the genetic association of type 2diabetes with these variants is confirmed.
these variants are not associated with the progression to diabetes.
the genetic variants in the present study do not appear to play an important role in the pathogenesis of type 2 Diabetes in Chinese population.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the genetic variants associated with type 2 diabetes are not necessarily causal variants for diabetes but may be associated with other metabolic traits.

we found that the novel variants identified in the GWAS are associated with quantitative traits in the same direction as in the original report, and that they are associated with progression to diabetes in the prospective cohort.

we identified several new genetic variants associated with type 2 diabetes, and we also identified several genetic variants associated with quantitative measures that may be useful in identifying subjects with a higher risk for diabetes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the genetic variants associated with type 2 diabetes are not only associated with diabetes but also with the metabolic syndrome and related quantitative traits.

the variants associated with diabetes are not necessarily associated with the risk of progression from prediabetes to diabetes, which suggests that the genetic variants are not directly related to progression of the disease.
the genetic variants associated with diabetes are not associated with fasting glucose, but are associated with insulin sensitivity.
